podcast.title: My brother's suit

hosts.Leyla: lives in Baku and loves a good plan
hosts.Sam: grew up in Manchester and once travelled with no plan at all

before.predict: Do you wear clothes from your family? Guess: who in this episode went to a job interview in a suit that was too big — Leyla or Sam?

chapters.title: The suit that did not fit

lines.t: Hi everyone, and welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
And I'm Sam. Today's topic is fashion and style. And I'm wearing my best shirt for it.
[laugh] I noticed. Very smart. Is it new?
No, it's a hand-me-down from my older brother. Most of my wardrobe is his old clothes.
That's actually very good. It's sustainable fashion.
It was not so good for my first job interview. I wanted to dress to impress, so I borrowed his suit.
And?
He's ten centimetres taller than me. The jacket didn't fit at all. The sleeves covered my hands.
Oh no! Did you get the job?
I did! The manager smiled and said, "Nice suit. Is it your dad's?"
[laugh] For me, it's the opposite story. I buy almost nothing new now. I go to second-hand shops.
Really? Why?
Every trend comes and goes so fast. Something is in fashion for one season, and then people throw it away.
True. And cheap clothes off the rack often fall apart after a few washes.
Exactly. So I buy fewer things, but better ones. One good brand of jeans that lasts five years.
What about accessories?
That's my secret. One simple outfit, and then a different accessory every day — a scarf, earrings, a bag. It always looks new.
Clever. My only accessory is my watch. And it's also my brother's.
[chuckle] Your brother has very good style, then.
He does. I just have his old style, five years later.
Here's your question for your next SpeakLab call: what is your favourite piece of clothing — and what's the story behind it?
Mine is this shirt. Thanks, brother. See you next time!
Bye for now!
